title: Business Central base application tables: customers, vendors, items, open and posted sales documents, purchase documents, the general, customer and item ledgers and dimension sets
status_note: Written on 17 November 2026 in our own words. Table numbers and field names were checked against Microsoft Learn's base application table reference (ms.date 2024-10-01); those pages show neither keys nor FlowFields nor table relations, which were read in Microsoft's AL source of the base application (microsoft/BCApps at a pinned commit; first-party, not Learn). Table names are the AL names in upper case with underscores (SALES_HEADER for Sales Header, G_L_ENTRY for G/L Entry); columns likewise, compared without case or punctuation, so the SQL spelling (Document No_) and the bc2adls one (DocumentNo-6) are read alike. Not verified against any company's rows. Krusgraph is independent and not affiliated with Microsoft.

variants.bc_sql: The per-company SQL tables <company>$<table>$<app id> (a database copy, Business Central on premises), dots as underscores.
variants.bc2adls: An export with bc2adls: <Table>-<id> tables and <Field>-<id> columns, letters and digits only, with $Company.

The order a posted invoice came from. Business Central declares no table relation, the order is usually deleted once fully shipped and invoiced, and Sales Header's key also needs Document Type = 1 (Order): listed so the column is read for what it is, not applied.
Only lines whose TYPE is Item (2, or Item as text).
Only lines whose TYPE is Item (2, or Item as text).

A set has one row per dimension: the join repeats each ledger entry once per dimension in its set. Filter DIMENSION_CODE to one dimension (the codes are the company's own) before joining; listed, not applied.
As for G/L Entry: one row per dimension in the set; filter DIMENSION_CODE first. Listed, not applied.

traps.title: Header amounts are FlowFields: they are not in the export
traps.text: Sales Header, Sales Invoice Header and Purchase Header show Amount and Amount Including VAT, and Cust. Ledger Entry shows Amount and Remaining Amount, but these are FlowFields computed from other tables when read; they are not stored, and an export of the tables (bc2adls refuses them) has no such column. Sum the lines (Sales Line, Sales Invoice Line) or Detailed Cust. Ledg. Entry. A header amount column in a landing was computed by whoever landed it: check what it sums before adding it to the lines.

traps.title: Every table is per company
traps.text: Business Central keeps data per company by default: in SQL each company has its own table (<company>$Customer$<app id>), in an export or mirror the companies' rows sit side by side with the company in a column ($Company in bc2adls). Customer C10000 can exist in every company: a key, a join or a sum without the company mixes companies. When the company is a column, keep it in every key and join; when it is in the table name, union the companies' tables with the company as a column first (the pack recognises one table per name).

traps.title: Open documents of every kind share one table
traps.text: Sales Header and Sales Line hold quotes, orders, invoices, credit memos, blanket and return orders, told apart by DOCUMENT_TYPE; No. is unique only within a type. A sum over Sales Line without a filter on DOCUMENT_TYPE adds quotes to orders; a credit memo's amounts are positive although they reduce revenue. Posted invoices are in Sales Invoice Header/Line, not here.

traps.title: No. on a line is an item only when TYPE says so
traps.text: Sales Line, Sales Invoice Line and Purchase Line carry TYPE and No.: the number is a G/L account, an item, a resource, a fixed asset, an item charge or an allocation account according to TYPE. Join No. to Item only for TYPE Item (2).

traps.title: One posted invoice appears in several ledgers
traps.text: Posting a sales invoice writes Sales Invoice Header/Line, a Cust. Ledger Entry with its Detailed Cust. Ledg. Entries, G/L Entries for revenue, VAT and receivables, and Item and Value Entries for the items. Each is a view of the same money: revenue comes from one of them, never from their union. G/L amounts are in LCY with debit positive, so revenue is negative there.

traps.title: Joining a dimension set repeats the entry
traps.text: DIMENSION_SET_ID on an entry matches one Dimension Set Entry row per dimension. Join with a filter on one DIMENSION_CODE, or pivot the dimensions first.

traps.title: How the names arrive depends on the route
traps.text: In SQL: <company>$<table>$<app id> with dots as underscores (Cust_ Ledger Entry, Document No_). In bc2adls: <Table>-<id> and <Field>-<id> with letters and digits only (CustLedgerEntry-21, DocumentNo-6) and a $Company column. Through the APIs (the Power Query connector, Dataflow Gen2): API entities such as salesOrders keyed by the SystemId GUID, not by No. The Fabric mirroring pages do not say how the mirror names tables and columns. The pack reads the SQL and bc2adls spellings; the API entities are not described here.
